chk_problem.reason: Both drafts describe the core problem of melody-preserving lyric editing in singing voice synthesis, focusing on selective preservation of reference characteristics while changing lyrics.

chk_method.reason: Both drafts identify the same core components of the method: State-Control-Transition (SCT) and Progressive State-Control Grounding (PSCG).

chk_data.reason: Both drafts list the exact same training datasets and hours (8,000 hours Mandarin singing, 2,000 hours Mandarin Emilia speech, and 300 hours curated open-source singing).

chk_setup.reason: Draft A describes the training hyperparameters (seeds, updates, optimizer, batch size), whereas Draft B describes the evaluation protocol and benchmarks.

chk_primary_result.reason: Both drafts report the same primary result of a 46.2% reduction in macro-PER compared to the Vevo2 baseline, with Draft B providing additional specific numbers.

chk_secondary_result.reason: Both drafts report the same improvements in naturalness (+0.48 N-MOS) and lyric intelligibility (+0.32 L-MOS) over YingMusic+.

chk_baseline.reason: Both drafts identify the same baselines: Vevo2 (discrete autoregressive) and YingMusic+ (continuous non-autoregressive).

chk_conclusion.reason: Both drafts conclude that CLASVS successfully establishes a continuous autoregressive foundation for melody-preserving lyric editing.

chk_limitation.reason: Both drafts identify the same limitations: evaluation restricted to Mandarin 2-6-syllable edits, with cross-lingual and long-edit validation remaining as open challenges.
